comparator.name: Bachelor Creative Technology
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme page defines twelve 15-EC modules across three years. Years one and two comprise eight themed modules. Module 5 requires one of three specialisations; Smart Technology is selected as the first option in the current official order, independently of UCR fit. Year three contains 30 EC of genuine minor, exchange, internship, education-minor or other elective space and a 30-EC graduation semester. The official current-student page resolves that graduation semester into Academic Writing (5 EC), Reflection (5 EC) and a two-part Graduation Project (20 EC). All components total exactly 180 EC.

alternatives.label: Creative computing, design & digital society
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines programming, data and AI with product design, user research, communication and the societal effects of technology.
alternatives.concept: A broad closest feasible Creative Technology response combining creative computing, data and AI with human-centred product design, communication, user evaluation, organisational change and responsible digital innovation.
progression: All formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned semester. Programming, data, business, research and mathematical foundations precede advanced design, algorithms, machine learning, evaluation and digital-innovation work; six 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: AI, data & smart systems
alternatives.labelReason: Four mathematics and systems courses replace four design, qualitative and organisational courses, making intelligent data-driven systems the differentiating strand.
alternatives.concept: A technical Creative Technology direction combining programming, data, AI and algorithms with mathematical modelling of systems, signals and uncertainty, while retaining product, communication and responsible-innovation context.
alternatives.distinctness: Linear Algebra, Computational & Numerical Methods, Linear Systems and Probability & Statistics replace Consumer Product Design, Qualitative Research Methodology, Psychology of Organizations & Leadership and Persuasive Communication. Each curriculum therefore contains 30 EC absent from the other.
progression: All formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned semester. Mathematical Methods precedes linear algebra, numerical methods, linear systems and probability; programming precedes algorithms and AI optimisation; six 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Human-centred interaction & technology
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum retains a technical foundation but adds a sustained psychology, cognition, sociology, interaction and communication sequence.
alternatives.concept: A human-centred Creative Technology direction studying perception, social behaviour, interaction, language, institutional trust and technology adoption alongside programming, data, product design and organisational innovation.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest programme, Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Social Psychology, Modern Sociology, Perception & Action, Higher Order Functions, New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory and Psycholinguistics replace Mathematical Methods, Logic & Discrete Mathematics, Qualitative Research Methodology, Ethics, Algorithms & Data Structures, Optimization Methods in AI and Neural Networks & Deep Learning. The 52.5-EC shift is human-centred and also exceeds the pairwise 30-EC floor against the smart-systems route.
progression: All formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned semester. Brain and behaviour precedes advanced cognition; sociology foundations precede advanced social theory; research and product foundations precede advanced interaction and evaluation; six 300-level courses are included.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Creative Technology bachelor. The current curriculum offers Smart Technology, Interactive Media and Designing Fair Futures as equally formal 15-EC specialisations and does not establish one as uniquely broad. Smart Technology is selected as the first option in the official order, independently of UCR fit.

selection.assessment: The broad closest response is feasible. The official AI/data/smart-technology and human-centred interaction strands each support a coherent additional curriculum with material course consequences. All three pass qualitative and pairwise 30-EC distinctness, so production stops at the permitted maximum.

blocks: Introduction to Programming addresses the programming foundation inside this broad introductory module, without reproducing its full multidisciplinary scope.
Introduction to Data Science addresses data processing and visualisation, while the comparator module additionally physicalises data through an installation.
Machine Learning directly addresses the AI and machine-learning core, without the comparator's dedicated-hardware project.
Linear Systems directly addresses systems, signals and control modelling in the selected Smart Technology specialisation, but not its sensors and electronics labs.
UCR has programming and design courses but no physical-computing, circuits, Arduino and smart-environment laboratory module, so this component remains unmatched.
Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations uses design thinking and external problem framing to develop and test solutions, overlapping an important function of this client-centred module.
Consumer Product Design directly develops user-needs analysis, prototyping and iterative evaluation, while the comparator focuses specifically on human-computer interaction.
AI Ethics provides structured reflection on human, societal and ethical consequences of designed technologies, while the comparator reflection component is broader.
Persuasive Communication studies framing, affect and audience response relevant to creating impact through interaction, but does not reproduce the comparator's art-installation practice.
The genuine 30-EC choice space is preserved without inventing a specific minor, exchange or internship.
UCR courses include substantial writing, but no selected course reproduces this dedicated graduation-project academic-writing component.
UCR's optional independent-research opportunity is shown separately against this compulsory 20-EC graduation project; it is not part of the fixed 180-EC UCR programme.

notes.text: Creative Technology integrates computer science, electrical engineering, physical computing, interactive media and studio-style design projects. UCR can build substantial related programmes from programming, data science, AI, mathematics, product design, cognition, communication, sociology, business and ethics, but it does not offer the comparator's electronics, sensors, Arduino, fabrication and integrated installation-lab sequence.
